Fish and Lumber in New England

options.misconception: Virginia's share was about 40% — large, but smaller than South Carolina's 70%.
New York's share was about 20% — the smallest of the three shares given.
The table gives New England only a small share, with no number at all.

rationales.A: The table's last column gives the enslaved share of the population around 1740: about 40% of Virginia, about 20% of New York, and about 70% of South Carolina. Seventy percent is the largest share, so South Carolina is the answer. Background: rice plantations in the Lower South depended on enslaved African labor, and by 1740 enslaved people outnumbered free people there.
rationales.B: Virginia's share was about 40% — large, but smaller than South Carolina's 70%.
rationales.C: New York's share was about 20% — the smallest of the three shares given.
rationales.D: The table gives New England only a small share, with no number at all.
rationales.general:
1. Find the last column. It gives the enslaved share of the population around 1740.
2. Read down the column. Virginia about 40%, New York about 20%, South Carolina about 70%.
3. Compare the numbers. Seventy is the largest of the three.
4. Name the place. South Carolina, in the Lower South, where rice plantations ran on enslaved labor.
Remember: when a table hands you numbers, compare them before you reason about them.

source: original; stimulus is an original data table compiled from the grounding books
stem: According to the table, where were enslaved people the largest share of the population around 1740?

stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from the grounding books; see grounding.
stimulus.text:
| Region | Leading exports | Labor | Settlement | Enslaved people, c. 1740 |
| Chesapeake (Virginia, Maryland) | Tobacco | Enslaved Africans and indentured servants | Scattered plantations along rivers | About 40% of Virginia's population |
| New England | Fish, timber, ships | Free families on small farms | Compact towns | A small share, mostly household and skilled work |
| Middle Colonies | Wheat, grain, livestock | Free labor, with some enslaved workers | Farms and towns | About 20% of New York's population |
| Lower South (South Carolina, Georgia) | Rice and indigo | Enslaved Africans | Large plantations | About 70% of South Carolina's population |
